question: Should Crabline intentionally ship the direct-only WhatsApp group rejection and the new `libsignal` runtime dependency in its production package?
rationale: Accepting an existing-workflow break and a new cryptographic execution dependency requires maintainer intent beyond automated correctness review.

options.title: Approve with safeguards
options.body: Confirm direct-only fail-closed behavior, complete dependency and licensing review, remove the changelog entry, and merge after final checks pass.

options.title: Replace the dependency
options.body: Keep the behavioral hardening but implement Signal-session handling through an already-approved dependency or existing internal primitive.

options.title: Preserve group compatibility
options.body: Retain current group-target behavior by default and expose direct-only rejection only through an explicit strict policy.

recommendation.title: Approve with safeguards
recommendation.body: Confirm direct-only fail-closed behavior, complete dependency and licensing review, remove the changelog entry, and merge after final checks pass.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the proposed implementation and are the only organization member connected to this code in the supplied evidence.
